narration_lines: A place floods when water comes in faster than it can flow away.
A low-lying area is low ground. Water slides there and fills it first.
Two houses on one street can have different elevations. The lower one sits in water first.
Ground that is already wet takes in new rain slowly. Rain that comes faster stays on top.
A drain can only carry so much water. This limit is its drainage capacity. Extra rain waits on the street.
When the water level in the river is higher than the canal, its gate closes. Pumps push the water out instead.
Flood water is patient. It recedes when the drains and rivers have room again.
People read a staff gauge to watch the water level. Rising or falling is the big question.
Next time a puddle grows, we can ask: where can this water go?
